claim.markdown_says:
b) If there is no SHARING clause in that file control entry,

   1\. If an OPEN statement for the associated file connector has a SHARING phrase, ...

   2\. If an OPEN statement for the associated file connector has no SHARING phrase, ...
claim.why_it_matters: The markdown indents items 1. and 2. at the same level as a) and b), flattening the nesting; the sub-items read as siblings of b) rather than as its children. Wording is intact.

verdict.reasoning: The observation is accurate but it is only indentation. The printed page (ISO/IEC 1989:2014 p.259, PDF p.283) indents items 1. and 2. one level deeper than a) and b). In page-283.md lines 23-29, a), b), 1\. and 2\. all carry the same 3-space indent; none of them is a Markdown list, since the numbers are escaped. Every word is present and in order. The hierarchy can still be read from the text: b) ends with a comma and has no consequent of its own, and the items use a different numbering style (1./2. against a)/b)). So 1. and 2. can only be read as the completion of b), and the meaning of GR1 is unchanged. Under the rejection criteria (formatting only, meaning unchanged), the claim is not a content discrepancy.
